description: Turn engineering calculations into AI-callable tools with CalcTree. Discover pages in a workspace, execute them with custom inputs via simpleCalculate, and build new ones. MathJS and Python statements with real unit handling.
rules: Read skills/calctree/SKILL.md first, and REFERENCE.md for the exact GraphQL documents: it is verified against the live API and supersedes any older CalcTree documentation

To use a CalcTree page as a tool: (1) list_workspace_pages to discover pages, (2) get_page_context to introspect inputs and outputs, (3) simple_calculate with scope overrides to execute with custom inputs

simple_calculate takes scope: [{name, value}] where values are MathJS-serialised strings like '10 m' or '50 kN / m'. It returns recomputed namedValues for every statement. calculationId equals the page id
One 'x-api-key' header covers everything: reads, simpleCalculate (tool execution), page creation, insertMDXContent and createOrUpdateCalculation. Verified live 2026-08-21
An invalid or empty API key surfaces as a GraphQL 'Unexpected error.' with no 401 and no mention of auth: check the key before debugging anything else
Values arrive MathJS-serialised: unit quantities as { mathjs: 'Unit', value: 8, unit: 'm' }, plain numbers, booleans, strings, matrices
Dataset variables (VLOOKUP) are NOT included in the simpleCalculate scope — they always report 'Undefined symbol' even when the dataset works in the UI
Creating a page takes two steps: create it, then register it in the page tree. A page that exists but is not in the tree is orphaned and invisible
The calculation id equals the page id. Include the page id when creating a calculation or it will not be visible on any page
Revision ids are KSUIDs. The platform's latest-revision sentinel is '~', which sorts above every base62 character. Hex-looking values such as 'ffffffff' are fragile: do not use them
Evaluation is asynchronous: settle about two seconds after a write before reading, or a read can return zero statements
Verify calculations by reading the page context (statements with namedValues and errors), never by reading the page back as MDX: MDX round-trips prose but returns calculation blocks empty
Engine types: mathjs (single statement), multiline_mathjs (multiple statements), python, excel, dataset, connection. All statements in a calculation share one scope
MathJS formulas use assignment syntax 'variable = expression'. Put units on inputs ('load = 5 kN'); calculated values inherit them. Unit arithmetic is automatic (1 kPa * 1 m^2 = 1 kN)
Never name a variable after a unit abbreviation (N, V, Pa, M, mm, m, s, kg, K, A, g, h, d, J): a variable named mm shadows the millimetre unit and nulls every later conversion on the page
A pass/fail check must be a named boolean, never a string ternary: 'check = util <= 1 ? "PASS" : "FAIL"' is always truthy, so a traffic-light chip renders green whatever the result
Escape < and > as < and > everywhere including prose: a raw one truncates the MDX import from that point on

Show a computed value in prose with a mention link, which renders inline with the value's unit: [fctm](mention:variable:fctm:format="number",decimal="2",showTitle="false",showValue="true",variableType="number"). Round for display with decimal on the mention, not in a rounded copy of the value. Do not write the legacy <Mention> tag: it renders as a block and breaks the sentence

MathJS variables with units arrive in Python as ct.quantity() objects already: do not wrap them again. Create new ones with ct.quantity('100 kN'), convert with .to('unit'), and read the number with .magnitude (a property, not a method)
Never put an offset unit (degC, degF) in scope on a page with a Python cell: it fails the whole cell with 'Ambiguous operation with offset unit'
Deleting a page is a soft delete: trashed pages still return from the pages query

In-place content edits cannot remove or reorder body nodes, and leave old statements behind so variables end up defined twice and the page nulls out. To replace content, delete the page and re-create it
Page URLs follow the format https://app.calctree.com/edit/{workspaceId}/{pageId}
insertMDXContent now sets statement titles from the MDX name attribute automatically (fixed 2026-08-24). No separate title pass is needed
